Superintendent Wayne Barker told the school board Monday that he hopes this academic year’s group of NACS Community Ambassadors will be the first of many. “Ultimately, our goal is to create this network of people who have a deep understanding of what happens here in our school district and have them help to share our story,” Barker said. “It’s my hope that this will be a program that exists in 2046.” Participation is open to local parents, business owners, retirees, volunteers and civic leaders, he said. No expertise in education is required. Other districts, including Southwest Allen County and Warsaw Community schools, have offered similar programs. For NACS, Barker said, the initiative will advance two focus areas of its strategic plan: community and belonging, and trust and transparency. Participants will explore various aspects of district operations, including curriculum development, the budgeting process and food services. Classroom visits, facility tours and open dialogue with district leaders are among the hands-on experiences planned. The learning should go both ways. Barker described the program as an opportunity to gather feedback from the ambassadors and “learn from them to drive improvements.” NACS’ application form is available at www.nacs.k12.in.us/nca . It asks prospective ambassadors to describe their motivation for applying, their connections to the district and the areas they are most interested in learning about, among other questions. The form also asks if applicants can attend all nine sessions, explaining that is essential to obtain the full value of the experience. Most activities are planned for the third Thursday of the month. The application deadline is Aug. 14. Barker expects 15 to 20 people will be chosen. “We want it to be big enough that it’s meaningful but yet small enough that it’s manageable,” he told the board. The elected officials had their first August meeting in the morning instead of the evening because of back-to-school preparations and events. Students will return to NACS classrooms Wednesday. asloboda@jg.net Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Barker Courtesy Schedule NACS Community Ambassadors sessions will meet from 7:45 to 9:30 a.m. at the NACS Administration Center, 12913 Coldwater Road. The dates and themes are as follows. Sept. 17 – Welcome to NACS: District history, traditions, strategic planning. Oct. 22 – Teaching and learning: Classroom visits, early learning initiatives, curriculum development and a student panel. Nov. 19 – Supporting every student: Special education services, mental health support, school counseling and high-ability programming. Dec. 17 – Discovering passions: Fine arts, athletic programs, career pathways and extracurricular opportunities. Jan. 21 – Making it possible: Tours of school safety, transportation, technology infrastructure, food services and facilities operations. Feb. 18 – Stewardship: School finance, human resources, state legislative effects and district budgeting processes. March 18 – Looking ahead: Community growth planning, construction updates, innovation and NACS Education Foundation. April 15 – Celebration of learning: Reflection on takeaways, discussions and preparation for community engagement. May 13 – Graduation and recognition More information Schools 101: Southwest Allen, Warsaw programs creates district advocates Southwest Allen County Schools parents ask Erin Nash questions about topics such as elearning and snow days as if she’s a district expert. http://www.austinglobe.com/news/27926675.text: Hungary labels Russia a threat RT.com 26 Aug 2026, 21:04 GMT+10 Budapest now considers Moscow a threat to Europe, in a major foreign policy shift by Prime Minister Peter Magyar Hungary considers Russia a "threat to Hungary, Europe and the global order," according to a foreign policy directive published by the country's new pro-EU government. The statement marks a dramatic shift from the pragmatic relations pursued by former Prime Minister Viktor Orban. Signed by Prime Minister Peter Magyar on Tuesday, the document states that "Hungary condemns Russian military aggression and fully supports Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders, and recognizes Ukraine's right to self-defense." "Russia's behavior poses a threat to Hungary, Europe and the global order, and also puts the Hungarian minority living in Transcarpathia in serious danger, therefore we support all efforts aimed at initiating negotiations towards sustainable peace and long-term security guarantees," it continued. Hungary had not formally designated Russia a "threat" at any point since 1945. This new position is almost identical to that of the EU, which also backs "sustainable peace and long-term security guarantees," but only if they recognize Kiev's maximalist demands - a return to Ukraine's 1991 borders, freedom for Ukraine to pursue NATO and EU membership, and NATO-like security guarantees provided by European and American forces. Since taking office in May, Magyar has worked to align Budapest's foreign policy with Brussels'. He has ended Hungary's opposition to EU accession talks with Ukraine, backed the bloc's 21st package of anti-Russian sanctions, and lifted Budapest's veto on a €90 billion loan package to Kiev. Magyar's predecessor, Viktor Orban, condemned Russia's military operation in Ukraine. However, he also condemned the "war policies" of the West that provoked the conflict, and refused to help arm Kiev, arguing that Ukraine cannot hope to defeat Russia and should seek an imperfect peace deal instead. Orban argued that the EU's self-imposed embargo on Russian energy would "kill off the European economy," and lent support to its sanctions packages only after securing exemptions that would allow Hungary to continue purchasing Russian oil, gas, and nuclear fuel. Hungary still imports energy from Russia under Magyar. Andrei Kolesnik, a member of Russia's State Duma committee on defense, Andrei Kolesnik, suggested that Russia could cut these supplies in response. "They've given [Magyar] the order to now treat Russia poorly," he told Gazeta.ru. "They're trying to gain some benefits. I think that oil supplies to Hungary, and energy supplies to Hungary from Russia, are now in question after such statements." Orban's government viewed Kiev, not Moscow, as the most pressing threat to Ukraine's Hungarian minority. Under Vladimir Zelensky's rule, ethnic Hungarians in Transcarpathia have had their language rights restricted and been subjected tobrutal forced conscription. In June, Magyar struck what he called a "formal agreement" with Zelensky to protect the rights of Ukraine's ethnic Hungarians. However, no documents concerning the agreement have been published to date, making it completely unclear what protections Zelensky has agreed to. https://www.politico.eu/article/anne-wid.text: British authorities have charged a man accused of murdering former lawmaker Anne Widdecombe with planning a terror attack against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage. Counterterrorism police on Friday charged Joshua Kerry, 28, with one count of preparation of terrorist acts, for an activity that took place sometime between May 2024 and July 2026. Widdecombe, a former Brexit Party MEP, Conservative minister and Reform spokesperson, died on July 9. Prosecutors said she was hit on the head with a hammer 21 times. Kerry was accused of her murder. Advertisement Advertisement Britain’s head of counter-terrorism policing Vicki Evans said the force had “been running a hugely intensive and complex investigation for some time,” adding: “The charge announced today is a result of the tireless work of investigators across the counter-terrorism policing network.” Kerry is set to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday. In August, the counter-terrorism force reopened a year-long investigation into an alleged firebomb attack against Farage’s home. “I know the new charges made today will be extremely concerning. My profound sympathies are with Nigel Farage and his family,” said British Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. “Let no one make any mistake: an attack on anyone in politics is an attack on us all.” A Reform official told the BBC : “This is exactly why Nigel needed £5m to protect his security for life.” Farage is facing a parliamentary watchdog probe into a £5m gift from a billionaire donor before he became an MP in 2024, previously claiming he needed the money to ensure his security.
